questions.question: How did CCN2 affect the lymphatic markers and growth-factor genes in primary LECs, and what happened at the highest tested dose?

options.A: Markers rose dose-dependently through 100 ng/mL, then fell sharply at 200 ng/mL; Vegfc, Vegfd and Flt4 also increased
options.B: Markers fell through 100 ng/mL and recovered at 200 ng/mL; only Kdr increased
options.C: Markers increased linearly through 200 ng/mL, while Vegfc and Vegfd were unchanged
options.D: Only Prox1 increased, and all lymphangiogenic factor transcripts decreased

questions.rationale: CCN2 increased Lyve1, Pdpn and Prox1 through 100 ng/mL with a marked decline at 200 ng/mL; Vegfc, Vegfd and Flt4 increased while Kdr did not.
questions.evidence_quote: The expression levels of Lyve1, Pdpn and Prox1 were increased by CCN2 in a dose-dependent manner up to 100 ng/mL; at 200 ng/mL, their expression levels dramatically decreased compared with levels at 100 ng/mL

questions.question: Which receptor-tyrosine-kinase response distinguished CCN2-treated LECs from the VEGF receptor pathway?

options.A: VEGFR2/3 phosphorylation was unchanged, while EGFR and EphB4 phosphorylation increased
options.B: VEGFR2/3 phosphorylation increased, while EGFR and EphB4 were unchanged
options.C: VEGFR2/3 and PDGFRα increased, while EGFR phosphorylation decreased
options.D: All receptor tyrosine kinases tested were phosphorylated equally

questions.rationale: The phospho-RTK array found no activation of VEGFR2/3 despite increased EGFR and EphB4 phosphorylation.
questions.evidence_quote: VEGFR2 and VEGFR3 phosphorylations were unchanged by CCN2

questions.question: Which integrin perturbation most directly supported partial mediation of CCN2-induced ERK phosphorylation?

options.A: Integrin αv knockdown partially reduced phospho-ERK (p=0.0040)
options.C: Integrin β1 knockdown eliminated total ERK protein (p=0.0040)
options.D: Integrin β3 knockdown increased ERK only in vehicle-treated cells

questions.rationale: Suppression of integrin αv partially decreased CCN2-induced pERK relative to non-target siRNA, supporting its role in signaling.
questions.evidence_quote: Knockdown of integrin av by siRNA partially decreased phosphorylated ERK induced by CCN2 compared with non-target siRNA (p=0.0040)

questions.question: What unexpected result followed integrin β1 suppression, and what compensation did the authors rule out?

options.A: Basal phospho-ERK increased; β2 and β3 transcript levels did not increase to compensate
options.B: Basal phospho-ERK decreased; β2 and β3 expression doubled
options.C: CCN2-induced phospho-ERK increased; αv expression compensated for β1 loss
options.D: Total ERK declined; β3 phosphorylation compensated for β1 loss

questions.rationale: β1 suppression raised phospho-ERK, but the authors did not observe compensatory increases in integrin β2 or β3 mRNA.
questions.evidence_quote: phospho-ERK was increased by suppression of integrin b1 (p=0.05)

questions.question: How did CCN2 affect LEC proliferation across the measured times, and at what doses was a vehicle comparison significant at 24 h?

options.A: It weakly suppressed growth at 24 h; 50 and 100 ng/mL were significant versus vehicle, with no proliferation change at 48 or 72 h
options.B: It increased growth at 24 h at all doses, but not at 48 or 72 h
options.C: It suppressed growth at every time point, significantly at 10 ng/mL only
options.D: It had no effect at 24 h but increased growth at 48 and 72 h

questions.rationale: CCN2 showed a weak early growth-inhibitory effect; the 50 and 100 ng/mL conditions were significant versus vehicle only at 24 h.
questions.evidence_quote: treatment with 50 and 100 ng/mL of CCN2 suppressed cell growth at 24 h compared with vehicle-treated LECs (p = 0.003 and 0.02).

questions.question: What temporal pattern did CCN2-induced phospho-ERK show in LECs?

options.A: It increased by 15 min, continued rising to 4 h, declined at 8 h, then rose again after 48 h
options.B: It remained unchanged until 8 h, then declined through 48 h
options.C: It peaked at 15 min and fell steadily to baseline by 4 h
options.D: It rose only after 48 h and was absent at earlier times

questions.rationale: The time course showed an early increase, continued increase through four hours, an eight-hour decrease, and later increase by 48 hours.
questions.evidence_quote: phospho-ERK was significantly increased in LECs at 15 min after treatment with CCN2 and continued to increase up to 4h, followed by a decrease at 8 h, and increase after 48 h

questions.question: How did CCN2 affect the ERK–DUSP6 interaction, and what was the effect of DUSP6 knockdown on phospho-ERK?

options.A: CCN2 enhanced co-precipitation of DUSP6 with ERK; DUSP6 knockdown increased pERK after CCN2
options.B: CCN2 disrupted ERK–DUSP6 binding; DUSP6 knockdown reduced pERK
options.C: CCN2 increased DUSP6 binding only to total ERK, with no change in pERK after knockdown
options.D: CCN2 had no effect on binding, but DUSP6 knockdown eliminated total ERK

questions.rationale: Immunoprecipitation showed enhanced interaction under CCN2, and siRNA suppression of DUSP6 increased phosphorylated ERK.
questions.evidence_quote: The results showed that DUSP6 co-precipitated with ERK, and their interaction was enhanced by CCN2

questions.question: What in vivo evidence supported CCN2-induced lymphangiogenesis in the Matrigel plug experiment?

options.A: CCN2 plugs contained more Podoplanin-positive vessels and areas, with tubular structures
options.B: Control plugs had more Podoplanin-positive vessels and lower ERK phosphorylation
options.C: CCN2 plugs contained only CD31-positive blood vessels and no lymphatic markers
options.D: CCN2 reduced the number of vascular cavities but increased fibroblast staining

questions.rationale: Histology showed Podoplanin-positive tubular structures and increased vessel number and area in CCN2-containing plugs.
questions.evidence_quote: The number of Podoplanin-positive vessels and percentage of Podoplanin-positive areas were increased in CCN2-supplemented gels compared with controls

questions.question: Why did the authors caution against treating their in-vitro proliferation and in-vivo Matrigel findings as contradictory?

options.A: ECM effects and MMP-mediated CCN2 processing in Matrigel may account for stronger in-vivo lymphangiogenesis
options.B: The in-vivo assay used human cells, whereas in-vitro assays used mouse LECs
options.C: The proliferation assay measured ERK, whereas Matrigel assays measured DUSP6 only
options.D: Matrigel results were not statistically significant and were excluded from interpretation

questions.rationale: They proposed the extracellular matrix and MMP processing of CCN2 as possible contributors to the differing contexts.
questions.evidence_quote: The discrepancy observed between the in vitro cell proliferation and in vivo Matrigel assays may be due to effects of ECM and matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) in Matrigel.

questions.question: What unresolved relationship did the authors identify among DUSP6 and the transcription factors FOXC1/FOXC2?

options.A: DUSP6 suppresses ERK in LECs, but its relationship to FOXC1 and FOXC2 was not analyzed
options.B: FOXC1 and FOXC2 directly induce DUSP6, as demonstrated by their siRNA experiments
options.C: DUSP6 is downstream of FOXC1 but independent of FOXC2 in lymphatic vessels
options.D: FOXC1/FOXC2 deletion reduces ERK and eliminates DUSP6 expression

questions.rationale: The study identified DUSP6 as an ERK suppressor but explicitly left its relationship with FOXC1/FOXC2 for future work.
questions.evidence_quote: the relationship between FOXC1, FOXC2 and DUSP6 has not yet been analyzed.
